rows.rationale: The amending instrument supersedes the original clause, changing the check meter threshold from 17.5 kW to 50 kWp. | The clause regarding transformer capacity limits does not support the rejection based on missing check meters.

The proposed capacity is 45.00 kWp, which is below the 50kWp threshold required for a check meter under KA-C5-006#cl-18. | The cumulative solar capacity (95kW) is 95% of the 100kVA transformer, but Note ii states installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible.
The rule mandates check meters for systems > 20 kW, but the application's sanctioned load is 25 kW, making the check meter requirement applicable despite the 20 kWp DC capacity.

The decision is premature because the technical feasibility outcome is still 'Not communicated by the licensee' per the DISCOM portal status. | The generator failed to consider the rule stating installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without a formal feasibility report.
The cited clause was superseded by GJ-C3-003, which requires 1.0 and 0.5S accuracy instead of 0.2s.

The generator cited an outdated capacity range (5-5000 kW) instead of the amended rule allowing up to 5 times sanctioned load (max 10 MW). | The generator failed to apply the 2024 amendment which permits 12000 kWp as it is within 5 times the 3000 kW sanctioned load and under 10 MW.
The 2015 regulations were superseded by the 2019 regulations as per the amending instrument. | The proposed 1.0 kWp capacity does not exceed the 2.0 kW sanctioned load, so rejection is incorrect.

The proposed 1.00 kWp capacity violates clause 5.1's proviso which requires a minimum capacity of 1 kWp, but the generator failed to address the 2015 regulation's minimum requirement. | The generator failed to consider UP-C3-001#cl-5.2 which mandates a minimum capacity of one kilowatt peak.
The amending instrument supersedes the cited clause, changing the check meter threshold from 17.5 kW to 50 kWp.
The generator cited a 50kWp threshold, but KA-C5-001#cl-15 mandates a check meter for systems exceeding 17.5 kW.

The system capacity is 12.00 kWp, which is below the 20 kW threshold where check meters become mandatory. | The cited accuracy class rule does not justify rejection as the proposed generation meter is class 2.0.
The rule states check meters are mandatory only for systems > 20 kW, but this system is 12 kWp.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 Amendment (DL-C3-015#cl-9.2b) which allows two changes per financial year instead of one. | The application shows 2 changes made, which is permitted under the current 2025 guidelines, making the rejection incorrect.
The rule limits changes to twice per financial year, and the application has already made two changes, meaning this third request is prohibited.

The generator cited a capacity range rule, but the application's Group Net Metering capacity must comply with the 5x sanctioned load limit per DL-C3-009#cl-3.8. | The 2024 amendment limiting GNM capacity to 5 times the sanctioned load was not considered in the decision.
The SLD waiver only applies to 11kV and below networks, but this project uses a 33 kV connection. | The cumulative capacity for BRPL is 50 MW, which is below the 75 MW threshold for the waiver.

The cited clause was superseded by DL-C3-015, which updated the cumulative capacity thresholds for TPDDL. | The application's TPDDL cumulative capacity is 105 MW, which is within the updated 110 MW threshold, making the rejection incorrect.

The 2015 regulations were superseded by the 2019 regulations (UP-C3-002). | The 2019 regulation allows 75% capacity, and the current load (125/160 = 78.1%) exceeds this, but the generator cited the wrong, superseded rule.

The generator cited an outdated capacity limit, whereas the 2024 amendment allows capacity up to 5 times the sanctioned load (500 kW) for this 100 kW load. | The generator failed to apply the 2024 amendment which permits a 500 kW capacity for a 100 kW sanctioned load.

The proposed 600 kWp capacity exceeds the 5x sanctioned load limit (500 kW) specified in the applicable DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 guidelines. | The generator failed to apply the 5x sanctioned load limit rule which restricts the capacity to 500 kW for this 100 kW load.
The proposed 600 kWp capacity exceeds the 5x sanctioned load limit of 500 kW (100 kW * 5) allowed under the cited rule.

The generator approved the application based on SDO verification, but the technical feasibility outcome is still 'Not communicated by the licensee'. | The rule stating installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without a report should have been used to justify approval despite the pending status.

The restrictive definition in DL-C3-006 was superseded by DL-C3-015, which makes VNM applicable to all consumers in NCT of Delhi. | The cited clause regarding capacity limits does not support the rejection based on consumer category.
The clause expands VNM applicability to all consumers, which supports the user's request rather than justifying a rejection.

The cited clause states MSME capacity is irrespective of sanctioned load, contradicting the rejection based on a 50% limit. | This clause pertains to connectivity voltage levels and does not support a capacity-based rejection.
The generator approved the application based on a rule for systems >20kW, but the proposed capacity is 18.00 kWp, making check meters optional.
The generator approved the application despite the EPC proposal lacking a check meter, even though the 30kWp capacity requires one under the cited rule.

The generator cited a 50kWp threshold, but the correct threshold for check meters in Karnataka per KA-C5-001#cl-15 is 17.5 kW. | The generator failed to consider KA-C5-001#cl-15, which mandates a check meter for this 30kWp system.

The cited 65% limit was superseded by the amending instrument which removed the percentage cap, allowing cumulative capacity up to 100% of the transformer capacity. | Even under the old 65% rule, 85kW/100kVA is 85%, which exceeds 65%, but the rule itself is no longer valid per the amending text.

The cumulative capacity (85 kW) is within the 100 kW transformer limit, but the generator failed to check if it violates the 65% peak capacity limit mentioned in GJ-C3-001. | The 65% cumulative capacity limit for distribution transformers must be verified to ensure compliance with the original regulation.
The amending instrument supersedes the 65% limit with a new provision, and the current cumulative capacity (70kW) exceeds the transformer rating (100kVA) regardless of the percentage.

The cumulative capacity (70 kW) is within the transformer limit (100 kVA), but the generator failed to check the 65% limit specified in GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso. | The 65% peak capacity limit for distribution transformers must be verified against the cumulative solar capacity.

The application is still in the 'Technical Feasibility' stage and the outcome is 'Not communicated', so it cannot be approved yet. | The 9kWp proposal is deemed feasible under Note ii, but the generator failed to consider this rule to justify the status.
The generator approved the application despite the EPC proposal stating 'Solar Check Meter: Not provided', which violates the cited rule requiring a check meter for systems >17.5 kW.

The generator cited a 50kWp threshold, but KA-C5-001#cl-15 requires a check meter for systems exceeding 17.5 kW. | The generator failed to consider KA-C5-001#cl-15, which mandates a check meter for this 35kWp system.

The generator cites the old 0.2s accuracy requirement, but the amending regulation GJ-C3-003 allows 1.0 class for the Solar Generation Meter. | The generator failed to note that the Solar Check Meter is mandatory for systems >20kW, which this 25kWp system requires.

The proposed meters (1.0 and 0.5S) meet the accuracy requirements specified in the cited clause. | The system capacity is 25 kWp, making a check meter mandatory, but the rejection reason focuses on accuracy rather than the missing check meter.
The cited clause confirms eligibility for net billing up to 999 KW, yet the application is rejected despite being a domestic consumer with 8.0 kW sanctioned load.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 amendment (DL-C3-015#cl-3.2) which expanded VNM applicability to all consumers. | The generator used an outdated restrictive list for VNM instead of the current universal applicability rule.
The proposed 120 kWp capacity significantly exceeds the consumer's sanctioned load of 30.0 kW, which may violate capacity-to-load ratios under VNM guidelines.

The 65% threshold was superseded by an amendment stating cumulative capacity shall not exceed the transformer capacity. | Even under the old 65% rule, 55kW/100kVA is 55%, which is within limits, but the cited rule text is outdated.

The cumulative solar capacity (55 kW) is well within the transformer capacity (100 kVA), but the decision ignores the 65% peak capacity limit specified in GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso. | The 65% cumulative capacity limit rule was not considered in the generator's decision-making process.

The cited rule was superseded by DL-C3-015 effective 2026-01-20, which provides higher capacity thresholds for BRPL. | The generator used outdated capacity limits (75 MW) instead of the current 110 MW limit for BRPL.
The cited clause confirms eligibility for net billing up to 999 KW, yet the application is rejected despite being a domestic consumer with 4.0 kW load.

The 2015 regulations were superseded by the 2019 regulations as per the amending instrument. | The 2019 regulation allows 75% capacity, and the current transformer load (78/100 = 78%) exceeds this, but the generator cited the wrong rule.

The cited clause was superseded by the 2025 Amendment (DL-C3-015) which allows two changes per financial year instead of one. | While the rule allows two changes, the application failed both requirements: it is the second change and only provided one month's notice instead of two.
The amending instrument clarifies that claims for Phase II applications are admissible if received till 31.12.2025, making the 2026-02-16 claim valid.
The cumulative TPDDL capacity is 120 MW, which exceeds the 50 MW waiver threshold specified in the cited rule.
The cumulative capacity for TPDDL is 120 MW, which exceeds the 100 MW waiver threshold specified in the cited clause.
The generator cited an outdated requirement for 0.2s accuracy, whereas the amending instrument GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5-class specifies 1.0 and 0.5S accuracy.

The decision is premature because the technical feasibility outcome has not yet been communicated by the licensee as required by this clause. | The generator failed to consider that installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible, which would support an approval if the feasibility stage were complete.
The amending instrument clarifies that claims for Phase II applications are admissible if received till 31.12.2025, making the October 2024 deadline obsolete.

This clause was superseded by the 2025 amendment (DL-C3-015#cl-3.2) which expanded VNM applicability to all consumers in NCT of Delhi. | The decision fails to account for the 5x sanctioned load limit (30kW * 5 = 150kW) vs the proposed 200kWp capacity.

The cited clause confirms VNM applicability, which supports the user's request rather than justifying a rejection. | The clause defines capacity limits for VNM, but the generator failed to show the 200kWp exceeds the 5x sanctioned load limit (150kWp).
